anterior-pituitary-hormones.moa: Growth hormone acts through IGF-1; ACTH stimulates the adrenal cortex; TSH stimulates the thyroid; FSH and LH act on the gonads; prolactin acts on the breast
anterior-pituitary-hormones.uses: Growth hormone: growth failure and GH deficiency; ACTH: diagnostic test of adrenal function; FSH, LH and hCG: infertility and ovulation induction; TSH: thyroid cancer scanning
anterior-pituitary-hormones.adr: Growth hormone: oedema, joint pain, glucose intolerance; gonadotropins: ovarian hyperstimulation and multiple pregnancy; ACTH: Cushingoid effects
anterior-pituitary-hormones.ci: Growth hormone: active tumour and closed epiphyses; gonadotropins: ovarian cysts, undiagnosed bleeding and hormone-dependent tumours

drugs-altering-anterior-pituitary-hormon.moa: Octreotide and lanreotide (somatostatin analogues) and pegvisomant (GH receptor blocker) lower GH; bromocriptine and cabergoline (D2 agonists) lower prolactin; GnRH analogues (leuprolide, goserelin) suppress gonadotropins when given continuously; metoclopramide and domperidone raise prolactin; clomiphene raises gonadotropins
drugs-altering-anterior-pituitary-hormon.uses: Acromegaly; hyperprolactinaemia and prolactinoma; prostate cancer, endometriosis and precocious puberty (GnRH analogues); ovulation induction (clomiphene); lactation suppression
drugs-altering-anterior-pituitary-hormon.adr: Bromocriptine: nausea, postural hypotension, psychosis; octreotide: gallstones and diarrhoea; GnRH analogues: hot flushes, bone loss and an initial flare; clomiphene: hot flushes, multiple pregnancy and visual symptoms
drugs-altering-anterior-pituitary-hormon.ci: Bromocriptine: severe heart disease and pregnancy hypertension; clomiphene: ovarian cysts, liver disease and pregnancy; GnRH analogues: pregnancy

thyroid-hormone.moa: Levothyroxine (T4) and liothyronine (T3) bind nuclear thyroid receptors and raise gene transcription, increasing metabolic rate, heart rate and growth
thyroid-hormone.uses: Hypothyroidism, myxoedema coma, congenital hypothyroidism, goitre, suppression in thyroid cancer
thyroid-hormone.adr: Overdose gives thyrotoxic symptoms: palpitations, tremor, weight loss, sweating and heat intolerance; angina and arrhythmias
thyroid-hormone.ci: Untreated adrenal insufficiency, thyrotoxicosis, recent MI; start with a low dose in the elderly and in heart disease; avoid taking with iron or calcium

thyroid-inhibitors.moa: Thionamides (carbimazole, methimazole, propylthiouracil) block thyroid peroxidase so hormone synthesis falls (PTU also blocks T4 to T3 conversion); iodide and iodine inhibit hormone release; perchlorate and thiocyanate block iodide trapping; radioactive iodine destroys thyroid tissue
thyroid-inhibitors.uses: Hyperthyroidism and Graves' disease; thyroid storm (PTU, iodide, propranolol); preoperative preparation; radioiodine for definitive treatment
thyroid-inhibitors.adr: Rash, agranulocytosis (sore throat and fever are warning signs), hepatitis (PTU), goitre and hypothyroidism; radioiodine: hypothyroidism
thyroid-inhibitors.ci: Pregnancy and lactation (radioiodine absolutely; carbimazole in the first trimester, use PTU then); history of agranulocytosis; iodide in iodine-sensitive patients

insulins.moa: Bind the insulin receptor (tyrosine kinase), increasing glucose uptake and glycogen and fat synthesis, and lowering blood glucose; analogues change the onset and duration
insulins.uses: Type 1 diabetes; type 2 diabetes when oral drugs fail; diabetic ketoacidosis; gestational diabetes; hyperkalaemia (with glucose); perioperative control
insulins.adr: Hypoglycaemia (the commonest: sweating, tremor, confusion), weight gain, lipodystrophy at injection sites, hypokalaemia, local allergy and insulin antibodies
insulins.ci: Hypoglycaemia; caution with β-blockers (mask symptoms); lower dose in renal failure; do not give intermediate or long-acting insulin intravenously; avoid thiazolidinediones with insulin in heart failure

oral-antidiabetic-drugs.moa: Sulfonylureas (glibenclamide, glimepiride) and meglitinides close K-ATP channels, releasing insulin; metformin lowers hepatic glucose output and improves sensitivity; glitazones (pioglitazone) activate PPARγ; α-glucosidase inhibitors (acarbose) delay glucose absorption; DPP-4 inhibitors (sitagliptin) raise incretins; SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin) cause glucosuria; GLP-1 agonists boost insulin and slow gastric emptying
oral-antidiabetic-drugs.uses: Type 2 diabetes, with metformin as first line; SGLT2 inhibitors also in heart failure and chronic kidney disease
oral-antidiabetic-drugs.adr: Sulfonylureas: hypoglycaemia and weight gain; metformin: GI upset, lactic acidosis and B12 deficiency; glitazones: fluid retention and fractures; acarbose: flatulence; SGLT2 inhibitors: genital infections and ketoacidosis; GLP-1 agonists: nausea and pancreatitis
oral-antidiabetic-drugs.ci: Type 1 diabetes and ketoacidosis; metformin in renal impairment, liver failure, hypoxia and around contrast studies; sulfonylureas in pregnancy and severe renal or liver disease; glitazones in heart failure

corticosteroids.moa: Glucocorticoids bind intracellular receptors and change gene expression: they inhibit phospholipase A2 and cytokines, reduce inflammation and immunity, and raise blood glucose; mineralocorticoids (fludrocortisone) retain sodium and lose potassium
corticosteroids.uses: Adrenal insufficiency replacement; asthma, allergy and anaphylaxis; autoimmune and inflammatory diseases; organ transplant; cerebral oedema; leukaemias and lymphomas; antenatal steroids for foetal lung maturity
corticosteroids.adr: Cushingoid appearance, hyperglycaemia, hypertension, osteoporosis, peptic ulcer, infections, cataract and glaucoma, myopathy, mood changes, growth retardation in children, adrenal suppression on sudden stopping
corticosteroids.ci: Active untreated infection, systemic fungal infection, peptic ulcer, uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension, osteoporosis, psychosis; live vaccines in high doses; never stop abruptly after prolonged use

topical-steroids.moa: Anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive and vasoconstrictor actions in the skin; potency ranges from mild (hydrocortisone) to very potent (clobetasol)
topical-steroids.uses: Eczema, psoriasis, dermatitis, lichen planus and other inflammatory skin diseases; use the weakest effective potency for the shortest time
topical-steroids.adr: Skin atrophy, striae, telangiectasia, acne, hypopigmentation, delayed healing, masking of infection (tinea incognito); systemic absorption in children and over large areas
topical-steroids.ci: Untreated bacterial, viral or fungal skin infection; rosacea and perioral dermatitis; potent steroids on the face, groin and in children

androgens-and-related-drugs.moa: Testosterone acts on androgen receptors (and after conversion to DHT); anabolic steroids favour protein building; antiandrogens (flutamide, cyproterone, spironolactone) block the receptors; finasteride and dutasteride inhibit 5α-reductase
androgens-and-related-drugs.uses: Testosterone for hypogonadism; anabolic steroids in wasting (rare); antiandrogens in prostate cancer and hirsutism; finasteride in BPH and male-pattern baldness
androgens-and-related-drugs.adr: Androgens: acne, hirsutism, salt and water retention, polycythaemia, cholestatic jaundice, virilisation in women, premature epiphyseal closure in children, infertility; antiandrogens: gynaecomastia, impotence and liver injury (flutamide)
androgens-and-related-drugs.ci: Prostate or breast cancer (androgens), pregnancy, children and liver disease; finasteride: pregnant women must not handle crushed tablets

drugs-for-erectile-dysfunction.moa: PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) stop cGMP breakdown so nitric oxide causes penile vasodilation; alprostadil acts through prostaglandin E1; papaverine relaxes smooth muscle; testosterone corrects hypogonadism
drugs-for-erectile-dysfunction.uses: Erectile dysfunction; sildenafil and tadalafil also for pulmonary arterial hypertension; tadalafil for BPH symptoms
drugs-for-erectile-dysfunction.adr: Headache, flushing, dyspepsia, nasal congestion, visual disturbance (blue tinge), back pain; priapism; rarely sudden hearing or vision loss
drugs-for-erectile-dysfunction.ci: Nitrates and nicorandil (severe hypotension), recent MI or stroke, severe hypotension or heart failure, retinitis pigmentosa, penile deformity, and with ritonavir (reduce the dose)

estrogens-and-related-drugs.moa: Estrogens bind nuclear receptors in many tissues; antiestrogens (clomiphene) and SERMs (tamoxifen, raloxifene) act as antagonist or agonist depending on the tissue; fulvestrant degrades the receptor; aromatase inhibitors (anastrozole, letrozole) stop estrogen synthesis
estrogens-and-related-drugs.uses: Menopausal symptoms and osteoporosis; hypogonadism; contraception; breast cancer (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors, fulvestrant); raloxifene for osteoporosis; clomiphene for ovulation induction
estrogens-and-related-drugs.adr: Estrogens: nausea, breast tenderness, fluid retention, venous thromboembolism, endometrial cancer if unopposed, gallstones; tamoxifen: hot flushes, endometrial cancer and thrombosis; aromatase inhibitors: bone loss and joint pain
estrogens-and-related-drugs.ci: Estrogens: breast or endometrial cancer, thromboembolism, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, active liver disease and pregnancy; tamoxifen: thromboembolic disease and pregnancy

progestins.moa: Bind progesterone receptors to convert the endometrium to a secretory state, thicken cervical mucus and suppress ovulation; antiprogestins (mifepristone) block the receptor; selective modulators (ulipristal) act partially
progestins.uses: Contraception; dysfunctional uterine bleeding; endometriosis; hormone therapy with estrogen; endometrial cancer; mifepristone with misoprostol for medical abortion; emergency contraception
progestins.adr: Breast tenderness, weight gain, mood change, irregular bleeding, acne (19-nortestosterone group), headache; masculinisation of a female foetus (some drugs); mifepristone: bleeding and cramps
progestins.ci: Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, breast cancer, severe liver disease, thromboembolism and pregnancy (most); mifepristone: ectopic pregnancy, adrenal failure and long-term steroid use

hormonal-contraceptives.moa: Combined pills (estrogen and progestin) suppress ovulation, thicken cervical mucus and thin the endometrium; progestin-only pills and injectables (DMPA) act mainly on mucus and ovulation
hormonal-contraceptives.uses: Contraception; also menstrual regulation, dysmenorrhoea, acne, hirsutism, endometriosis and PCOS
hormonal-contraceptives.adr: Nausea, breast tenderness, spotting, headache, weight and mood change, hypertension, venous thromboembolism, a slight rise in breast and cervical cancer risk; DMPA: amenorrhoea, delayed return of fertility and bone loss
hormonal-contraceptives.ci: Combined pills: smokers over 35 years, thromboembolism, stroke or heart disease, migraine with aura, breast cancer, liver disease, pregnancy, undiagnosed bleeding and the first 6 weeks of breastfeeding; enzyme inducers (rifampicin, phenytoin) reduce the effect

uterine-stimulants.moa: Oxytocin acts on uterine oxytocin receptors; ergometrine and methylergometrine act on α and 5-HT receptors causing sustained contraction; prostaglandins (carboprost, dinoprostone, misoprostol) soften the cervix and contract the uterus
uterine-stimulants.uses: Induction and augmentation of labour; prevention and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage; completion of abortion; cervical ripening
uterine-stimulants.adr: Oxytocin: water intoxication, hypotension, hyperstimulation, uterine rupture and foetal distress; ergometrine: hypertension, vasospasm and nausea; carboprost: bronchospasm and diarrhoea
uterine-stimulants.ci: Foetopelvic disproportion, abnormal foetal presentation, foetal distress and previous uterine scar (labour induction); ergometrine: hypertension, pre-eclampsia, heart disease and before delivery of the baby; carboprost: asthma

uterine-relaxants.moa: β2 agonists (ritodrine, terbutaline, salbutamol) relax the myometrium through cAMP; nifedipine blocks calcium entry; atosiban blocks oxytocin receptors; magnesium sulphate and indomethacin have limited use
uterine-relaxants.uses: Delay preterm labour for about 48 hours to allow steroids to work; foetal distress due to uterine hyperstimulation; external cephalic version
uterine-relaxants.adr: β2 agonists: maternal tachycardia, tremor, palpitations, hypokalaemia, hyperglycaemia and pulmonary oedema; nifedipine: flushing, headache and hypotension; indomethacin: premature closure of the ductus; atosiban: nausea
uterine-relaxants.ci: Cardiac disease, severe pre-eclampsia, antepartum haemorrhage, chorioamnionitis, uncontrolled diabetes or hyperthyroidism (β2 agonists) and foetal death

skeletal-muscle-relaxants.moa: Peripherally acting: non-depolarising blockers (tubocurarine, atracurium, vecuronium, rocuronium) compete with acetylcholine at the motor end plate; the depolarising blocker succinylcholine persistently depolarises it; dantrolene blocks calcium release in muscle; Centrally acting: baclofen (GABA-B agonist), diazepam, tizanidine and methocarbamol reduce spinal reflexes
skeletal-muscle-relaxants.uses: Neuromuscular block during surgery and intubation; ICU ventilation; baclofen and tizanidine for spasticity; dantrolene for malignant hyperthermia; centrally acting drugs for muscle spasm and back pain
skeletal-muscle-relaxants.adr: Respiratory paralysis (needs ventilation); histamine release and hypotension (tubocurarine, atracurium); succinylcholine: hyperkalaemia, malignant hyperthermia, muscle pains and raised intraocular pressure; baclofen: drowsiness and weakness; dantrolene: liver toxicity
skeletal-muscle-relaxants.ci: Myasthenia gravis (non-depolarising drugs); succinylcholine in burns, crush injury, spinal cord injury, hyperkalaemia and a family history of malignant hyperthermia; aminoglycosides potentiate the block

local-anaesthetics.moa: Block voltage-gated sodium channels from the inside of the nerve membrane and stop conduction; small and myelinated pain fibres are blocked first
local-anaesthetics.uses: Surface, infiltration, nerve block, spinal and epidural anaesthesia; dental procedures; lidocaine also for ventricular arrhythmias; adrenaline is added to prolong the effect
local-anaesthetics.adr: Systemic toxicity: perioral numbness, tinnitus, restlessness and convulsions, then CNS depression, hypotension and cardiac arrest (bupivacaine is the most cardiotoxic); allergy with esters; methaemoglobinaemia (prilocaine, benzocaine); spinal: headache and hypotension
local-anaesthetics.ci: Known allergy; infection at the site; adrenaline-containing solutions at fingers, toes, ear and penis; heart block (lidocaine); bupivacaine for IV regional block; coagulopathy for spinal or epidural
